name: Woodpecker
summary: Cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform priced by contacted prospects — unlimited team seats and email accounts, built-in warm-ups, deliverability tooling and a lead finder.
best_for: outbound teams that want usage-priced cold email plus LinkedIn outreach, with unlimited seats and email accounts included instead of per-user fees
skip_if: you send occasional one-off campaigns (usage pricing only wins when you actually use it), or your motion is LinkedIn-heavy — $29 per connected account adds up
honest_knock: The $7-per-100-prospects unit reads cheap, but a real outbound motion stacks add-ons fast. Every connected LinkedIn account is $29 a month, managed sending addresses $6 a month apiece and extra warm-ups $5 per account — and contacted prospects are the meter, so scaling outreach scales the bill.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month minimum entry (500-prospect minimum at $7.00 per 100 contacted prospects)
pricing.notes:
(price re-verified 2026-09-18 and again 2026-10-05 against woodpecker.co/pricing) Free trial: the pricing page and its FAQ put it at 14 days or 100 cold emails, whichever comes first (read 21 September 2026), and Woodpecker's partner team told us the same day that sign-ups through a partner link such as ours start on 30 days instead — their statement, dated, not something we have run through a fresh account. Usage-priced: $7.00 per 100 contacted prospects, and the smallest volume the slider offers is 500 — so $35 a month is the practical entry rather than the $7 headline. Contact 200 prospects and you still pay $35; the per-100 figure only starts describing your bill once you are past that minimum. Unlimited team members and unlimited connected email accounts are included, and the page prices in twelve currencies (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, AUD, BRL, CAD, DKK, INR, NOK, PLN, SEK). An annual toggle advertises SAVE 33% against monthly.

The sending allowance is derived, not chosen: the page states that emails per month equal contacted prospects multiplied by 16, the maximum number of campaign steps, which puts the 500-prospect entry at 16,000 emails a month. Add-ons are where an outbound motion actually gets expensive, and there are now two grades of managed sending address rather than one: LinkedIn accounts $29 a month each; email addresses on Google or Microsoft $6 a month each; email addresses on Maildoso, Mailforge, Infraforge or Azure $4 a month each; extra warm-ups $5 a month per email account; new domains at roughly $1 a month per domain, billed annually, which the page flags as an approximation because it depends on the domain name and shows the exact price before payment. Lead Finder credits start at 500 for $10. The rest of the add-on list, read 5 October 2026: Infraforge dedicated servers $59 a month per server, Azure domain hosting $20 a month per domain, domain transfers $1 a month per domain billed annually, the integrations line (API, webhooks, MCP, CLI) at $20 a month, an agency panel at $27 a month per active client with white label at $5 a month per active client, and outbound workshops at $2,000 one-time for four two-hour sessions, $500 per extra session. Prices exclude VAT.

Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Hosted remote server at api.woodpecker.co/mcp/v1: paste the URL into your AI client, sign in to Woodpecker and approve — no API key and no local server. Manage campaigns, prospects, email sequences, mailboxes and campaign reporting in natural language, and set each tool to run automatically, ask for approval, or not at all. A local Docker build authenticated with an API key exists as well, and their docs name it the only route to Agency client accounts: the hosted server cannot select an account managed under an Agency.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their pricing page lists MCP Server inside the paid Integrations add-on, next to Claude, Clay, API, Webhooks and CLI — not in the base plan. The docs page itself states no plan.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
